questions.q: When did Nigeria gain independence from Britain?
questions.e: Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960.

questions.q: Which city was Nigeria's capital before Abuja?
questions.e: Lagos was the capital until the move to Abuja in 1991.

questions.q: Who was Nigeria's first Prime Minister?
questions.e: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa led the government at independence.

questions.q: Who became Nigeria's first President when the country became a republic?
questions.e: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe ("Zik") became the first President in 1963.

questions.q: In which year did the Nigerian Civil War begin?
questions.e: The Civil War ran from 1967 to 1970.

questions.q: Who was Nigeria's head of state when the Civil War ended in 1970?
questions.e: General Yakubu Gowon led Nigeria through the war.

questions.q: Which colonial administrator amalgamated Northern and Southern Nigeria in 1914?
questions.e: Frederick Lugard oversaw the 1914 amalgamation.

questions.q: When is Democracy Day celebrated in Nigeria?
questions.e: Since 2019, 12 June is Democracy Day (it used to be 29 May).

questions.q: Which British writer and journalist is credited with suggesting the name "Nigeria"?
questions.e: Flora Shaw proposed the name in 1897.

questions.q: In what year did Nigeria become a republic?
questions.e: Nigeria became a republic on 1 October 1963.

questions.q: In which year was the capital officially moved from Lagos to Abuja?
questions.e: The move was decided in 1976 and made official in December 1991.

questions.q: Who was Nigeria's first military head of state (1966)?
questions.e: General Aguiyi-Ironsi took power in January 1966.

questions.q: Who designed the Nigerian national flag?
questions.e: Taiwo Akinkunmi, a student, designed the green-white-green flag in 1959.

questions.q: Whose actions sparked the 1929 Aba Women's War?
questions.e: An Igbo woman, Nwanyeruwa, resisted an unfair tax count and sparked the protests.

questions.q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
questions.e: Abuja is Nigeria's capital city.

questions.q: What are the colours of the Nigerian flag?
questions.e: The flag has green, white and green vertical stripes.

questions.q: Which ocean borders Nigeria's southern coast?
questions.e: Nigeria sits on the Gulf of Guinea, part of the Atlantic.

questions.q: How many states does Nigeria have (not counting the FCT)?
questions.e: Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory.

questions.q: Which great river gave Nigeria its name?
questions.e: The name Nigeria comes from the River Niger.

questions.q: Which country does NOT border Nigeria?
questions.e: Nigeria borders Benin, Niger, Chad and Cameroon.

questions.q: Zuma Rock, the "Gateway to Abuja", is a famous...
questions.e: Zuma Rock is a huge monolith near Abuja.

questions.q: Which Nigerian city is known as the "Coal City"?
questions.e: Enugu got the name from its coal mining history.

questions.q: Yankari Game Reserve is in which state?
questions.e: Yankari National Park is in Bauchi State.

questions.q: Olumo Rock is a famous tourist site in which city?
questions.e: Olumo Rock stands in Abeokuta, Ogun State.

questions.q: Which lake lies on Nigeria's north-eastern border?
questions.e: Lake Chad is shared by Nigeria, Niger, Chad and Cameroon.

questions.q: Which Nigerian city is called the "Garden City"?
questions.e: Port Harcourt is nicknamed the Garden City.

questions.q: Which Nigerian state is the largest by land area?
questions.e: Niger State is the largest state by area.

questions.q: Which is Nigeria's highest mountain?
questions.e: Chappal Waddi in Taraba State rises about 2,419 metres.

questions.q: Which Nigerian state is the smallest by area?
questions.e: Lagos State is the smallest in land area.

questions.q: Which Nigerian dish is made from rice, tomatoes and pepper and loved all over West Africa?
questions.e: Jollof rice is a party favourite in Nigeria.

questions.q: Suya is best described as...
o: Spicy grilled meat on a stick
questions.e: Suya is thinly sliced meat grilled with yaji spice.

questions.q: Which festival celebrates the harvest among the Igbo?
questions.e: The New Yam Festival (Iri Ji) marks the harvest.

questions.q: The Durbar festival is famous for what?
questions.e: Durbar features parades of horsemen in northern Nigeria.

questions.q: What does "E kaaro" mean in Yoruba?
questions.e: "E kaaro" is the Yoruba morning greeting.

questions.q: What is the colourful head wrap worn by many Nigerian women called?
questions.e: The gele is an elegant head tie.

questions.q: The Argungu festival is famous for...
questions.e: The Argungu Fishing Festival takes place in Kebbi State.

questions.q: The Eyo festival, with masquerades dressed in white, is held in which city?
questions.e: Eyo masquerades parade on Lagos Island.

questions.q: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is in which town?
questions.e: The grove in Osogbo honours the river goddess Osun.

questions.q: Which instrument is known as the Yoruba "talking drum"?
questions.e: The dundun can imitate the tones of speech.

questions.q: In Hausa, what does "Sannu" mean?
questions.e: "Sannu" is a common friendly greeting.

questions.q: The famous Benin Bronzes come from which ancient kingdom?
questions.e: The bronzes were made in the Kingdom of Benin (Edo).

questions.q: Nok culture, known for terracotta sculptures, comes from which part of Nigeria?
questions.e: The Nok culture flourished in central Nigeria over 2,000 years ago.

questions.q: Who founded the Dangote Group?
questions.e: Aliko Dangote built Africa's largest cement empire.

questions.q: Who was the first Nigerian to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.e: Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel "Things Fall Apart"?
questions.e: Chinua Achebe published it in 1958.

questions.q: Who pioneered Afrobeat music?
questions.e: Fela Anikulapo Kuti created Afrobeat.

questions.q: Who wrote "Half of a Yellow Sun"?
questions.e: The novel is set during the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.q: Which Nigerian became Director-General of the World Trade Organization in 2021?
questions.e: She was the first woman and first African to lead the WTO.

questions.q: Who was the famous Nigerian women's rights activist and mother of Fela Kuti?
questions.e: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti campaigned for women's rights.

questions.q: What is the currency of Nigeria?
questions.e: The naira is divided into 100 kobo.

questions.q: Which is the most populous country in Africa?
questions.e: Nigeria has the largest population in Africa.

questions.q: What are the Super Eagles?
questions.e: The Super Eagles are Nigeria's national football team.

questions.q: Which animals appear as the supporters on Nigeria's coat of arms?
questions.e: Two white horses flank the shield, with an eagle on top.

questions.q: Which bird is Nigeria's national bird?
questions.e: The black crowned crane is the national bird.

questions.q: Which flower is Nigeria's national flower?
questions.e: Costus spectabilis, the yellow trumpet flower, is the national flower.

questions.q: Lagos is the capital of Nigeria.
questions.e: The capital is Abuja. Lagos is the biggest city.

questions.q: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa.
questions.e: Nigeria has the largest population on the continent.

questions.q: The River Niger flows through Nigeria.
questions.e: The River Niger runs through western Nigeria.

questions.q: Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory.
questions.e: That is 36 states and the FCT.

questions.q: Nigeria gained independence in 1963.
questions.e: Independence was in 1960; 1963 is when Nigeria became a republic.

questions.q: Zuma Rock is located in Lagos State.
questions.e: Zuma Rock is in Niger State, close to Abuja.

questions.q: The Nigerian flag has three vertical stripes.
questions.e: It is green, white and green, arranged vertically.
